candidates.buyer: Firms and institutions with their own boreholes: bottlers, farms and agri-hubs, car dealers, hotels, forestry camps
candidates.evidence: Eight July 2025 arrêtés on sgg.cg, e.g. https://www.sgg.cg/textes-officiels/arretes/2025/congo-arrete-2025-2052.pdf, -2053, -2055, -2058, -2059. The holders are mostly mid-size firms (BEAC, CFAO, IFO Interholco), not quiet family firms. Number of holders and whether smaller sites are enforced is unknown.
candidates.existing: No dedicated tool found; I did not search for competitors in a dedicated query.
candidates.name: Autonomous water production permit and abstraction-fee tracker (boreholes)
candidates.trigger: Law 13-2003 (water code), Decree 2008-85, arrêté 18018/2012 (procedure), arrêté 5169/2019 (abstraction fee). Permit is 5 years, renewable, non-transferable; borehole meter required; fee with 10% late surcharge, 100% on non-payment; ownership change notified within 15 days to the water regulator.
candidates.unchecked: Number of permit holders, who enforces metering, fee amount, whether small borehole owners are chased, any regulator portal. The PDF fetch returned binary only, so the text was read from search snippets.

candidates.buyer: Small industrial operators and gas, bakery, brewery and workshop owners holding pressure vessels; and the approved inspection bureaux
candidates.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
candidates.evidence: https://www.sgg.cg/JO/2011/congo-jo-2011-08.pdf and https://www.sgg.cg/JO/2018/congo-jo-2018-14.pdf (snippets only). Enforcement level, number of equipment owners and the list of approved bureaux not found. No lift rule found.
candidates.existing: None found; no competitor-specific search run.
candidates.name: Pressure-equipment (boiler, compressor, gas cylinder/tank) inspection scheduler
candidates.trigger: Law 3-2011 (16 Feb 2011): operator must arrange inspection periodique and requalification by a bureau conseil agréé approved by the mines minister; a 2018 arrêté (JO 2018 no. 14) sets 3, 5 or 10-year intervals for gas equipment and a minimum 3-year external/internal check for fixed vessels.
candidates.unchecked: Full law text, operator register duty, approved bureaux list, enforcement, equipment count, LPG cylinder rules (group B category 21).

candidates.buyer: Temporary-work agencies, subcontractors, and small firms (often foreign-owned shops, restaurants, construction firms) employing foreign workers
candidates.evidence: https://fr.allafrica.com/stories/202605300040.html (circular); https://liziba.cg/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/Decret-n°-2019-168-du-1er-juillet-2019-portant-approbation-des-statuts-de-lagence-congolaise-pour-lemploi.pdf. The new rule affects many firms at once, but it is a one-off permit process and the circular is a snippet only.
candidates.existing: Immigration consultants and EOR providers (Safeguard Global, Newland Chase) serve large employers; no local small-firm tool found.
candidates.name: Foreign-worker local-preference and ACPE validation manager
candidates.trigger: Ministry of Employment circular of 28 May 2026: recruiting, retaining or renewing a foreign worker requires ACPE-validated proof that no equivalent national skills exist. ACPE (decree 2019-168) validates contracts, issues work cards and controls private placement firms.
candidates.unchecked: Recurring versus one-off duty, ACPE online portal, fees, number of affected small firms, whether a deadline exists.

candidates.buyer: Private crèches, garderies and orphanages in Brazzaville (about 200 crèches and 30+ orphanages identified in 2024)
candidates.evidence: https://adiac-congo.com/print/content/mise-en-garde-154186 (snippet). Strong non-compliance, but willingness to pay is likely very low and the approval is a one-off file, not recurring.
candidates.name: Crèche and orphanage provisional-approval tracker
candidates.trigger: Jan 2024 Ministry of Social Affairs warning that most crèches and orphanages lack the approval required by law; only 5 of about 200 crèches and 6 of 30+ orphanages held provisional approval.
candidates.unchecked: Approval criteria, renewal cycle, fees, enforcement after 2024, whether other cities have the same issue.

candidates.evidence: https://sgg.cg/JO/2026/congo-jo-2026-39.pdf (snippet). Number of schools, inspection and learner-register duty unknown.
candidates.name: Driving-school approval and register compliance
candidates.trigger: Ministry of Transport grants approval school by school by arrêté (e.g. arrêtés 2786 and 2787, JO 2026 no. 39, 14 Sept).
candidates.unchecked: Criteria, renewal, learner records, number of schools.

candidates.buyer: Associations managing markets domaniaux (Ouenzé, Total, Poto-Poto) and the traders paying them
candidates.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
candidates.evidence: https://fr.allafrica.com/stories/202601060227.html and https://adiac-congo.com/print/content/contribuables-162577. The state or mairie may build its own system; the structuring rules are not yet published.
candidates.name: Domestic-market association tax and levy reporting
candidates.trigger: Jan 2026 Council of Ministers decision to structure taxes already collected in the markets (100 FCFA per day reported); Feb 2025 Brazzaville taxpayer census to build a reliable trader file and trace municipal receipts.
candidates.unchecked: Whether a new decree sets a reporting duty, who collects, whether the mairie system covers it.

candidates.buyer: 350+ pre-collection operators in Brazzaville (79% individual, informal); 250+ registered with the mairie via donor project
candidates.evidence: https://www.afd.fr/fr/projets/limiter-les-inondations-et-ameliorer-la-gestion-des-dechets-brazzaville and https://fr.allafrica.com/stories/202602050307.html. Data are 2014-2017 and donor-driven; the buyer is poor and informal.
candidates.name: Waste pre-collection operator registration and service log
candidates.trigger: Mairie authorisation with cahier des charges for operators (GRET/AFD design); Feb 2026 minister's plan to replace handcarts with modern equipment.
candidates.unchecked: Current licence rules, any reporting duty, whether reform changed the operator model. No septic desludging text found.

candidates.known_note: Same buyer group and duty as K03; new evidence only strengthens the trigger.
candidates.name: ACPE driver work card and DGSP compliance file for moto-taxi riders
candidates.trigger: Oct 2025 DGSP order (registration, helmet, numbered vests, no foreigners); Nov 2025 ACPE driver work card launch.

candidates.name: Household employer CNSS declaration
candidates.trigger: CNSS affiliation of domestic workers under conditions

candidates.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
candidates.name: Bureau de change licence reporting
candidates.trigger: Licensing by arrêté under CEMAC Regulation 02/18

candidates.buyer: Artisanal gold and diamond buyers, comptoirs
candidates.name: Gold and diamond buyer (comptoir) licence and Kimberley traceability
candidates.trigger: Mining ministry licensing and Kimberley Process traceability (2007 inspectors, certification bureau). Brazzaville texts not found.
candidates.unchecked: 2019 mining code and decrees on artisanal buying, current number of buyers, Kimberley status.

candidates.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
candidates.evidence: https://www.tuv.com/content-media-files/master-content/government-inspections-international-trade/congo/tuev-rheinland-republic-of-the-congo-pcec-program-fr-06.pdf. No national dealer licensing text found; fertiliser arrêté found was Niger's.
candidates.name: Pesticide and fertiliser dealer licence (CEMAC homologation)
candidates.trigger: CEMAC common pesticide registration regulation; PCEC conformity certificate on regulated imports (ACONOQ).
candidates.unchecked: National dealer licence, register of sales, whether fertilisers are on the PCEC list.

candidates.name: Ferrous scrap dealers and export (Congo as transit for scrap to India)
candidates.trigger: Unknown Congo rule; Gabon banned scrap exports and a re-export route via Congo-Brazzaville was reported.
candidates.unchecked: Congo scrap licence or export rules; whether Congo followed Gabon.

coverage.category: 1. Household employers: domestic workers, live-in carers, nannies
coverage.found: Domestic workers are affiliated to CNSS only under unspecified conditions (africarrieres.com guide); no household-specific rule found. Nothing new beyond K04.

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: No Congo-Brazzaville scrap licensing found. Gabonmediatime reports an illegal ferrous-scrap export network to India routed via Congo-Brazzaville after Gabon's export ban (unverified for Congo rules). No candidate.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: Only used-vehicle and used-clothing import notes (see 5); no pawnbroker or second-hand register found.

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
coverage.found: No Brazzaville comptoir or jeweller rules found; results were DRC. Sangha gold rush (Chinese firms) and Kimberley diamond traceability bureau (2007, dated) only. Unverified.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: Used-car trade booming (about 40,000 used vehicles per year at Pointe-Noire, 2019 estimate); no dismantler or parts regime found. Age cap of 10 years only from a non-official exporter site. Unverified.

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: No domestic livestock transport or market rules found; the country imports its veterinary products and relies on imports for meat. Nothing found.

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: No Brazzaville abattoir or meat-inspection text found; results were DRC or other countries.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: No registration or reporting duty found; only NGO and WCS-supported beekeeping projects (Lac Télé, Likouala).

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: No Congo-Brazzaville veterinary order or pharmacy licence text found (OMSA/TRUVET 2026 slides say supply is import-only, regulatory framework needs strengthening). Unverified.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: Water code (Law 13-2003) and Decree 2008-85 require an arrêté authorisation for autonomous water production (5 years, renewable, personal, meter at borehole, abstraction fee under arrêté 5169/2019 with 10% late penalty). July 2025 arrêtés: LCDE, IFO Interholco, BEAC, CFAO Mobility, Go Fresh, TPT Investissement, ENE Congo, Global Développement. Holders are mid-size firms. One candidate. No driller licensing text found.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: Over 350 pre-collection operators in Brazzaville (79% informal, GRET); 250+ registered with the mairie under AFD/GRET Filipa; Feb 2026 minister wants to end handcart collection. No septic-tank desludging text found. One weak candidate.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: Law 3-2011 on pressure equipment: operator must have periodic inspection and requalification done by a 'bureau conseil agréé' approved by the mines minister; 2018 arrêté sets 3/5/10-year intervals for gas equipment. No lift rules found. One candidate.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: Mini-network distribution to third parties is expressly banned for autonomous producers (art. 96 water code, per 2025 arrêtés). No small-system operator regime found.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: CEMAC common pesticide registration regulation applies; PCEC conformity programme (ACONOQ) for regulated imports. No Congo dealer or applicator licensing text found. Unverified.

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: ACPE (decree 2019-168) controls private placement firms and validates contracts and work cards. Ministerial circular of 28 May 2026: hiring, keeping or renewing a foreign worker requires ACPE-validated proof of no equivalent national skills; applies to firms, subcontractors and temp agencies. One candidate.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: Only a 2018 arrêté creating a civil-registry centre at the Brazzaville funeral parlours. No funeral or cemetery licensing text found.

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
coverage.found: 1901-law declaration at prefecture, récépissé, JO publication fee 15,000 FCFA; registration reported as discretionary (2025 report). No annual reporting duty found. Weak.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: Oct 2025 DGSP order (registration, helmets, numbered vests, no foreigners, one passenger); Nov 2025 ACPE driver work card launch; driving-licence and grey-card drives in departments (Feb 2026). Nothing new beyond K03 and K10; the ACPE work card is a possible add-on to K03.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: Jan 2026 Council of Ministers decided to structure the taxes collected in domaniaux markets (100 FCFA per day in Ouenzé, Total, Poto-Poto); Feb 2025 Brazzaville taxpayer census. Bureaux de change: nothing new beyond K09. One weak candidate.

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
coverage.found: Jan 2024 Ministry of Social Affairs warning: of about 200 crèches identified in Brazzaville only 5 held provisional approvals (of 30+ orphanages, 6). Driving schools approved school by school by ministerial arrêté (JO 2026 no. 39: Quicky Business, Stan). Tattoo, food producers, hunting outfitters not searched.
